_about: Public-domain Samuel M. Janney, Quaker minister and historian of Virginia, for the Word Hoard: Conversations on Religious Subjects, An Historical Sketch of the Christian Church during the Middle Ages, his lives of William Penn and George Fox, his History of the Religious Society of Friends, An Examination of the Causes of the Separation, and his Summary of Christian Doctrines. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 133 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

janney-conversations: Conversations on religious subjects between a father and his two sons (Philadelphia : printed by John Richards, 1843)
janney-middle-ages: An historical sketch of the Christian church during the Middle Ages (Philadelphia, J. Richards, Printer, 1847)
janney-william-penn: The life of William Penn : with selections from his correspondence and autobiography (Philadelphia : Lippincott, Grambo, 1853)
janney-george-fox: The life of George Fox; with dissertations on his views concerning the doctrines, testimonies and discipline of the Christian church (Philadelphia Lippincott, Grambo, 1853)
janney-history-friends: History of the Religious Society of Friends, from Its Rise to the Year 1828 (Hayes & Zell, 1859)
janney-separation: An examination of the causes which led to the separation of the Religious Society of Friends in America, in l827-28 (Philadelphia : T. Ellwood Zell, 1868)
janney-summary-doctrines: Summary of Christian Doctrines as Held by the Religious Society of Friends (Friends' Publication Association, 1871)

_excluded.janney-poems: The Last of the Lenapé is poetry, outside this theology shelf
_excluded.janney-others: the Penn treaty addresses and delegates' report are by others
